questions.question: Describe the problem situation of the Term 1 PAT and explain why it matters beyond convenience.
questions.expected_answer: A new school building has a floor raised about 600 millimetres above the paving, reached only by an improvised step or stack of blocks. This is dangerous for everyone and impossible for a wheelchair user, a person with a pushchair or anyone unsteady. It matters because access to education is a right, public buildings must be accessible by law, and every learner should be able to enter alone and with dignity; the team acts as a building firm tendering to build proper stairs and a ramp.

questions.question: Map the five stages of IDMEC onto the ten weeks of the term and give the marks allocated to the assessed stages.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate in weeks 1 to 4, assessed in week 4 for 15 marks. Design in weeks 5 and 6, including the brief, sketches, evaluation and working drawings, for 20 marks. Make in weeks 7 and 8, the scale model, for 35 marks. Evaluate within design when choosing between ideas and after making when testing the model. Communicate in week 10, the tender presentation. The stages overlap but the main order holds, and all evidence goes in the PAT file.

questions.question: List what should be investigated at the site and among the users, and name three structural options with one strength or weakness each.
questions.expected_answer: Site: measure the rise at several points and use the largest, measure the space available for stairs and ramp, note the door swing, drainage and the ground type for foundations, and sketch with dimensions. Users: count peak use, ask the wheelchair user, the caretaker and the principal about needs and deliveries. Options: a straight ramp is simple but very long; a ramp that turns with a landing saves space but costs more; concrete on fill is durable but slow and heavy; steel framing is quick but needs corrosion protection; stairs may be one flight or two with a landing.
